title: What Credit Score Do Lenders Use for Business Loans?
summary: Most lenders check the owner's personal FICO score plus business scores like PAYDEX, Intelliscore Plus, Equifax and FICO SBSS, weighted by lender type, product and business age. Learn what each score measures, how the SBA's March 2026 SBSS change affects 7(a) loans, and how to build a multi-score credit policy.
body_markdown:
Lenders typically check the business owner's personal FICO score and then add one or more business credit scores. The common business scores are the Dun & Bradstreet PAYDEX, Experian Intelliscore Plus, Equifax business scores, and the FICO Small Business Scoring Service (SBSS). Which score carries the most weight depends on the lender type, the loan product, and how long the business has been operating.


A bank term loan, an SBA 7(a) loan, and a merchant cash advance (MCA) each weigh personal credit, business credit, and cash flow differently.[NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/business/loans/learn/minimum-credit-score) states that "there is no universal credit score minimum requirement for all business loans," and SBA rules changed in 2026. This guide covers personal vs. business credit, each scoring model, score use by lender type, and factors beyond scores. It ends with a framework for building a multi-score credit policy.


### Personal Credit vs. Business Credit for Business Loans


Personal and business credit scores answer different questions, which is why many lenders pull both. A personal score shows how the owner has handled consumer debt, while a business score shows how the company pays suppliers and creditors.


#### How Personal Credit Scores Work


Personal scores come from FICO and VantageScore and run on a 300 to 850 scale,[according to NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/business/loans/learn/minimum-credit-score) . NerdWallet also notes that lenders use the owner's personal score when reviewing business loan applications. Most published minimums for business loans refer to this personal score.


#### How Business Credit Scores Work


Business scores are built from commercial data such as trade payments, public records, and company demographics. Their scales differ by bureau and model, so an 80 from one bureau doesn't mean the same thing as an 80 from another.


#### How the Federal Reserve Groups Both Score Types


The Federal Reserve's[2026 Report on Employer Firms](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/-/media/project/clevelandfedtenant/fsbsite/reports/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms/2026-report-on-employer-firms.pdf) offers a useful reference point for comparing the two. For its survey analysis, the Fed classifies credit risk this way:


- **Low credit risk:** An 80 to 100 business score or a 720+ personal score
- **Medium credit risk:** A 50 to 79 business score or a 620 to 719 personal score
- **High credit risk:** A 1 to 49 business score or a personal score below 620


These are the Fed's analytic bands rather than lender cutoffs. Still, they show how the two score types roughly line up.


### Business Credit Scoring Models Lenders Use


Each business credit scoring model measures something different. Lenders should know what a score predicts before they set a threshold on it.


#### Dun & Bradstreet PAYDEX


PAYDEX is a dollar-weighted score that measures how promptly a business pays its vendors. It relies only on trade payments reported to Dun & Bradstreet. The[D&B PAYDEX fact sheet](https://www.dnb.co.uk/content/dam/web/data-and-ai/cross/content/paydex-score-factsheet/DnB_Paydex_Score_Factsheet.pdf) says trade references must fall within the last 24 months. The scale maps scores to payment timing:


- **100:** Payments made in anticipation of terms
- **90:** Payments made within discount terms
- **80:** Payments generally made within terms
- **70:** Payments made about 15 days beyond terms
- **50:** Payments made about 30 days beyond terms
- **0 to 19:** Payments made more than 120 days beyond terms


A PAYDEX of 80 means reported trade payments were generally on time, and a score above 80 means payments arrived early. It doesn't measure overall creditworthiness, debt load, or cash flow.


#### Experian Intelliscore Plus


Per[Experian's small business glossary](https://smallbusiness.experian.com/pdp.aspx?pg=glossary&bm=CREDITRANKING) , its business credit score, Intelliscore Plus, aims "to predict seriously derogatory payment behavior."


The 1 to 100 version groups scores into five risk bands:


- **76 to 100:** Low risk
- **51 to 75:** Low to medium risk
- **26 to 50:** Medium risk
- **11 to 25:** Medium to high risk
- **1 to 10:** High risk


Version matters here. Experian's[Intelliscore Plus V3 product sheet](https://www.experian.com/content/dam/marketing/na/assets/bis/business-information/brochures/intelliscore-plus-v3-ps.pdf) says V3 uses a 300 to 850 scale and projects risk over 24 months. The 1 to 100 bands don't apply to V3, so confirm which version a report shows before comparing scores.


#### Equifax Business Credit Scores


Equifax publishes more than one business score. Its Business Credit Risk Score runs from 101 to 992, and a higher score means lower risk,[per Chase for Business](https://www.chase.com/business/knowledge-center/start/business-credit-scores) .


Equifax also offers a separate Business Failure Score. Published ranges for it vary across sources, so confirm the scale on the report itself.


#### FICO Small Business Scoring Service (SBSS)


FICO SBSS is a blended score that runs up to 300, or 0 to 300[per Chase for Business](https://www.chase.com/business/knowledge-center/start/business-credit-scores) . Higher scores indicate lower credit risk,[according to CRS Credit API](https://crscreditapi.com/what-is-sbss-a-comprehensive-guide-for-small-business-lenders) . The[SBA's 7(a) program page](https://legacy.sba.gov/partners/lenders/7a-loan-program) says it combines consumer bureau data, business bureau data, borrower financials, and application data.


### Which Credit Score Lenders Use for Business Loans by Lender Type


The credit score lenders use for business loans shifts with the product and the lender's risk appetite. The personal-score figures below are typical ranges reported by[NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/business/loans/learn/minimum-credit-score) in August 2026. They are editorial generalizations rather than published lender policy, and individual lenders vary.


#### Banks and Credit Unions


NerdWallet reports that bank loans typically call for personal scores of about 680 to 700 or higher. In the[Fed's 2025 survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/-/media/project/clevelandfedtenant/fsbsite/reports/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms/2026-report-on-employer-firms.pdf) , 57% of employer-firm applicants to small banks were fully approved, compared with 43% at large banks. Those outcomes are self-reported, and firms chose where to apply.


#### SBA 7(a) Loans After the SBSS Sunset


For 7(a) Small Loans (up to $350,000) approved on or after March 1, 2026, the SBA no longer screens applications on the SBSS score.[SBA Procedural Notice 5000-876777](https://www.naggl.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/5000-876777.pdf) confirms SBA "will no longer screen 7(a) Small loan applications using the SBSS Score." Loans approved in E-Tran before 11:59 PM Eastern on February 28, 2026, may continue to use the SBSS score.


The SBA still expects real credit analysis. Lenders must follow prudent, generally accepted processes consistent with their similarly sized non-SBA commercial loans. The notice sets these requirements:


- **Scoring models:** Any model must be permitted by the lender's primary federal regulator and can't rely solely on consumer scores.
- **Documentation:** The credit memorandum must state the score and the acceptable approval range.
- **Cash flow:** The applicant's debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) must be at least 1.10:1, historical or projected.
- **Bank data:** Lenders must review the two most recent months of business bank activity or statements.


SBA Express loans are not affected, and SBA lenders may keep using business scoring models for them. The notice expires March 1, 2027, and SBA guidance continues to change, so lenders should check the current SOP before setting policy.


Some older content still cites an SBSS score of 165. Per[Whiteford, Taylor & Preston](https://www.whitefordlaw.com/news-events/client-alert-sba-issues-sop-50-10-8-key-changes-impacting-sba-7a-lending) , SOP 50 10 8 (effective June 1, 2025) used a 165 SBSS score for 7(a) Small Loan prescreening. That prescreening no longer applies to loans approved on or after March 1, 2026, even though SBA's legacy page still shows the figure.


On the personal side, NerdWallet reports that SBA lenders typically look for scores of about 620 to 680 or higher. NerdWallet also notes that[the SBA itself doesn't set a minimum credit score](https://www.nerdwallet.com/business/loans/learn/sba-loan-requirements) , so the minimum comes from each lender's credit policy.


#### Online Lenders


Online lenders commonly offer short-term loans and lines of credit. NerdWallet reports typical personal-score starting points of about 570+ for short-term loans and 600+ for lines of credit. In the[Fed survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/-/media/project/clevelandfedtenant/fsbsite/reports/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms/2026-report-on-employer-firms.pdf) , 38% of online lender applicants were fully approved, a self-reported figure that reflects who applies as much as lender standards.


#### Equipment Finance


NerdWallet reports that equipment financing typically starts around a 550+ personal score. Among the products in the[Fed survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/-/media/project/clevelandfedtenant/fsbsite/reports/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms/2026-report-on-employer-firms.pdf) , auto and equipment loans had the highest full approval rate, at 71%.


#### Merchant Cash Advances and Invoice Factoring


NerdWallet reports that MCAs and invoice factoring typically start around 500+, and MCA qualification leans heavily on revenue. Per[NerdWallet's MCA guide](https://www.nerdwallet.com/business/loans/learn/merchant-cash-advance) , new businesses and owners with poor credit may qualify with at least $10,000 in monthly sales. For MCAs, credit often shapes pricing more than eligibility.


[NerdWallet's Credibly review](https://www.nerdwallet.com/business/loans/reviews/credibly) shows how that works for one provider. Industry, years in operation, business financials, card transactions, and personal credit may all shape the factor rate.


### What Lenders Weigh Beyond Credit Scores


A credit score starts the conversation, but cash flow, business history, and guarantees often decide the outcome. Under[13 CFR § 120.150](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/13/120.150) , SBA lenders may consider the credit score or credit history of the applicant, its associates, and any guarantors. They may also consider earnings or cash flow and, where applicable, equity or collateral.


#### Cash Flow and Debt Service Coverage


DSCR compares the cash a business generates with its debt payments, and it is now an explicit SBA requirement. For 7(a) Small Loans approved on or after March 1, 2026, the applicant's DSCR must be 1.10:1 or higher. Recent business bank statements support that calculation.


#### Time in Business and Revenue


Older and larger firms were more likely to be fully approved in the[Fed's 2025 survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/-/media/project/clevelandfedtenant/fsbsite/reports/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms/2026-report-on-employer-firms.pdf) . Firms aged 0 to 5 years had a 48% full approval rate, compared with 63% for firms 21 years or older. Firms with revenue of $100,000 or less had a 37% rate, compared with 76% for firms above $10 million.


The Fed notes these figures aren't adjusted for profitability or credit risk, so they show correlation rather than cause. Business age also changes which score matters, because a young business may have few reported trade lines. Until business bureau files mature, lenders often lean more heavily on the owner's personal credit.


#### Personal Guarantees


Personal guarantees tie the owner's credit to the loan, which is one reason personal scores stay central. For SBA loans,[13 CFR § 120.160](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/13/120.160) says holders of at least 20% ownership "generally must guarantee the loan." Lenders may also require guarantees from others. In the[Fed's 2025 survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/-/media/project/clevelandfedtenant/fsbsite/reports/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms/2026-report-on-employer-firms.pdf) , 59% of employer firms with debt used a personal guarantee.


#### Why Applicants Report Being Denied


Low credit scores are one denial reason among several. The[Fed's 2025 survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/-/media/project/clevelandfedtenant/fsbsite/reports/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms/2026-report-on-employer-firms.pdf) asked employer-firm applicants not approved for at least some financing why they were turned down:


- **Lender requirements too strict:** 46%
- **Too much existing debt:** 37%
- **Low credit score:** 30%
- **Insufficient collateral:** 29%
- **Weak sales:** 29%


These answers are self-reported, respondents could pick more than one reason, and the Fed notes the survey is a convenience sample. Even so, they show that debt load, collateral, and sales matter alongside the score.


### How Lenders Can Build a Multi-Score Credit Policy


With the SBA's 2026 change, more of the scoring decision now sits with each lender. A documented policy that combines personal scores, business scores, and cash flow data helps teams decide consistently and explain each outcome. Here is a seven-step framework.


#### 1. Map Each Product to the Risk It Carries


List every product you offer, such as term loans, lines of credit, equipment financing, MCAs, factoring, and SBA loans. Then note what drives loss in each one, since a secured equipment loan and an unsecured line of credit carry very different risks.


#### 2. Choose a Primary and Secondary Score for Each Segment


Give each product and business-age segment a primary score and at least one supporting score. A young business may need personal FICO as the primary score. An established borrower with deep trade history can be weighted toward PAYDEX or Intelliscore Plus.


#### 3. Match Each Score to the Question It Answers


Use each model for what it actually predicts. PAYDEX covers vendor payment timing, Intelliscore Plus targets seriously derogatory payment behavior, and the Equifax Business Credit Risk Score adds a third bureau's view of risk. Treat them as complementary signals instead of interchangeable numbers.


#### 4. Document Approval Ranges and Model Versions


Record the acceptable range for each score, the model version, and the data date. SBA already requires 7(a) Small Loan lenders to state the score and approval range in the credit memorandum. The same discipline makes any credit policy easier to audit and defend.


#### 5. Add a Cash Flow Layer


Pair credit scores with bank statement analysis and a DSCR threshold. For SBA 7(a) Small Loans, the floor is 1.10:1 with two months of business bank statements. Cash flow checks also help lenders approve thin-file borrowers who can clearly repay.


#### 6. Set Guarantor and Collateral Rules


Define who must guarantee, whose personal credit you pull, and when collateral can offset a weaker score. For SBA loans, start with the 20% ownership rule and add any guarantors your policy requires.


#### 7. Route Declines and Recalibrate


Decide what happens when an applicant falls outside your ranges, such as a counteroffer, a different product, or a referral to another lender. Review approvals, declines, and loan performance regularly. Adjust thresholds when the data shows a range is too tight or too loose.

### Best Practices for Using Credit Scores in Business Lending


Most scoring mistakes come from comparing numbers that measure different things or from relying on outdated rules. These practices help lenders and borrowers avoid both.


#### Best Practices for Lenders


- **Never equate scores across bureaus:** A PAYDEX 80 and an Intelliscore Plus 80 measure different behaviors.
- **Record the model version:** Intelliscore Plus runs 1 to 100 in its earlier version but 300 to 850 in V3, per Experian.
- **Date-check SBA guidance:** The 165 SBSS prescreening score doesn't apply to 7(a) Small Loans approved on or after March 1, 2026.
- **Avoid consumer-only models for SBA:** A 7(a) Small Loan scoring model can't rely solely on consumer credit scores.
- **Treat published minimums as context:** NerdWallet's ranges are editorial benchmarks, so base thresholds on your own portfolio performance.


#### Best Practices for Borrowers


- **Check both credit types:** Review your personal credit and your D&B, Experian, and Equifax business reports before you apply.
- **Pay vendors within terms:** PAYDEX rewards on-time and early trade payments reported within the last 24 months.
- **Strengthen cash flow evidence:** Clean, recent bank statements support DSCR and revenue checks that can offset a weaker score.
- **Match the product to your profile:** NerdWallet reports lower typical personal-score minimums for equipment financing, factoring, and MCAs than for bank loans.


### Key Takeaways on Business Loan Credit Scores


Lenders typically check the owner's personal FICO score and add business scores such as PAYDEX, Intelliscore Plus, Equifax, or FICO SBSS. The mix depends on the lender, the product, and the business's age. NerdWallet's typical personal-score ranges start around 500+ for MCAs and factoring and reach 680+ for bank loans, but no universal minimum exists.


The biggest shift is at the SBA, which no longer screens 7(a) Small Loans approved on or after March 1, 2026, on SBSS. Lenders now document their own models and approval ranges and confirm a 1.10:1 DSCR. The key takeaway is that a documented, multi-score policy backed by cash flow data now matters more than any single number.

### Frequently Asked Questions About Business Loan Credit Scores


#### Do Lenders Check Personal or Business Credit for a Business Loan?


Many lenders check both, and the owner's personal score usually plays a role. Business scores carry more weight as a company builds trade history and bureau files.


#### Which Credit Bureaus Do Business Lenders Use?


For personal credit, lenders use FICO or VantageScore scores built from consumer bureau data. For business credit, the main sources are Dun & Bradstreet (PAYDEX), Experian (Intelliscore Plus), and Equifax. FICO SBSS blends consumer and business bureau data with borrower financials.


#### Can You Get a Business Loan With a Low Credit Score?


Yes, although your options narrow as scores fall. NerdWallet reports typical starting points of about 550+ for equipment financing and 500+ for invoice factoring and MCAs. MCAs also rely heavily on monthly sales.


#### What FICO SBSS Score Do You Need for an SBA Loan?


For SBA 7(a) Small Loans approved on or after March 1, 2026, the SBA doesn't screen on SBSS and sets no SBSS minimum. Lenders apply their own credit analysis and may still use SBSS or another permitted model. SBA Express loans can continue to use business scoring models.


#### Does Applying for a Business Loan Affect Your Credit Score?


It can, because many lenders pull the owner's personal credit during a full application. Ask each lender whether prequalification uses a soft inquiry and when a hard inquiry will happen. That lets you compare offers before a full credit pull.
